title: DIVE: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Interaction with Visual Engagement in Continuous Streams
abstract: arXiv:2610.28405v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially improved spoken interaction and video understanding. Existing online and streaming benchmarks primarily assess causal multimodal perception through timestamped question answering, whereas real-world interaction requires models to continuously identify task-relevant multimodal cues and decide whether, when, and how to respond. This leaves open how well current models can sustain real-time interaction throughout an evolving multimodal stream. To address this gap, we introduce DIVE, a benchmark for evaluating full-duplex interaction with visual engagement under continuous and realistic multimodal streams. It organizes six tasks into three complementary interaction scenarios. translated_title: DIVE：在连续流中评估具有视觉参与的全双工交互的基准
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的最新进展显著提升了口语交互和视频理解能力。现有的在线与流式基准主要通过带时间戳的问答来评估因果性的多模态感知，而真实世界的交互要求模型持续识别与任务相关的多模态线索，并决定是否、何时以及如何做出响应。这使得当前模型在动态演进的多模态流中维持实时交互的能力尚不清楚。为填补这一空白，我们提出了DIVE，一个用于在连续且真实的多模态流中评估具有视觉参与的全双工交互的基准。该基准将六项任务组织为三种互补的交互场景：（1）主动介入，评估模型能否识别新出现的视觉或语义线索，并在恰当的时机进行介入；（2）持续参与，评估模型能否进行持续的参……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出DIVE基准，将六项任务组织为三种互补场景（如主动介入与持续参与），以在连续真实的多模态流中评估多模态大模型进行全双工实时交互、判断何时以及如何响应的能力。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces DIVE, a benchmark that organizes six tasks into three complementary scenarios to evaluate full-duplex interaction with visual engagement in continuous multimodal streams, testing whether models can identify emerging cues and decide when and how to respond in real time.
